files.lesson.md: --- order: 13 unit: chance node: AC9M8P02 n2 uses: [AC9M8P02 n1, AC9M8P01 n2] title: And, or and not summary: "'A and B' means both happen; 'A or B' means at least one happens (both included); 'not A' is everything else. Read them from a Venn diagram, a two-way table or a grid, counting each outcome once." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A raffle prize goes to someone who plays sport or music. In a class of 30, 20 play sport and 13 play music. How many are in the draw?" connection: survey-two-way # data/connections/maths.yml (pilot: Make on paper and Also used in; documentation only) app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8331 url: http://127.0.0.1:8331/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: board.yml#explain-pic, caption: "Dog or cat: everything inside the circles, 9 + 4 + 6 = 19. The 4 with both are counted once." } explainClip: query: { code: "@board.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "And, or" say: "And is the overlap. Or is everything inside the circles." clip: - caption: { text: "Dog and cat: only the overlap, 4.", say: "Dog and cat is the overlap: four." } - click: Dog and Cat - wait: 1000 - caption: { text: "Dog or cat: add the rest of both circles. 19 of 30.", say: "Dog or cat is everything inside the circles: nineteen." } - click: Dog only - click: Cat only - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "19 of 30" } - wait: 1500 --- Probability questions often join events with **and**, **or** and **not**. On a Venn diagram, each one is a set of regions. ## Predict: sport or music ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to P(sport or music) shows whether they add the totals and count the overlap twice." check: type: predict q: "30 students: 20 play sport, 13 play music, 8 play both. What is P(a student plays sport or music)?" options: ["8/30", "25/30", "33/30"] actual: "25/30. 12 sport only, 8 both and 5 music only: each counted once. 33/30 counts the 8 twice (and a probability can't be more than 1)." ``` ## Run: choose the regions ```step stage: run insight: "Choosing 'or' on the diagram shows it is three regions, with the overlap counted once." try: { playground: board, starter: "board.yml#run", height: 560 } check: { type: board, text: "Choose the students who play sport or music. How many are there? Compare with your prediction.", when: "x = 1 and y = 1 and z = 1 and w = 0", explain: "Sport only, both and music only: 12 + 8 + 5 = 25, so P = 25/30 = 5/6." } ``` | Words | Regions | In the Sport and Music class | |---|---|---| | A **and** B | the overlap only | 8 | | A **or** B | anything inside the circles (one, the other, or both) | 12 + 8 + 5 = 25 | | **not** A | everything outside A | 5 + 5 = 10 | | **neither** | outside both circles | 5 | In maths, **or** includes both. In everyday talk "or" sometimes means one but not both ("tea or coffee?"); in maths that is **exactly one**. To find P(A or B) from totals, add them and take away the overlap once: 20 + 13 − 8 = 25. ## Investigate: counting once ```step stage: investigate insight: "'And' is one cell; 'or' adds the totals then takes the overlap once; adding the totals alone counts both twice (Zoe)." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "30 students: 13 have a dog, 10 have a cat and 4 have both. What is P(a dog and a cat)?" answer: "4/30" feedback: - ["23/30", "That adds dogs and cats. And means both: the overlap."] explain: "Both is the overlap: 4 of 30 = 2/15." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#zoe" text: "Zoe works out P(dog or cat) for the same class. Click the line where she goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: or-double-count explain: "Line 3: the 4 with both are in the 13 and in the 10, so they are counted twice. 13 + 10 − 4 = 19, so P = 19/30." - check: type: question q: "A dice is rolled. A is 'an even number' and B is 'more than 4'. Which outcomes are in A or B?" options: ["2, 4, 6, 5, 6", "5", "2, 4, 5, 6", "6"] answer: 2 feedback: ["6 is one outcome: list it once.", "That is B but not A.", null, "That is A and B."] explain: "Even: 2, 4, 6. More than 4: 5, 6. Either or both: 2, 4, 5, 6, so P(A or B) = 4/6." ``` ### And Here is the routine for "or" from totals. ```worked P(\text{juice}) = \tfrac{35}{60},\ P(\text{milk}) = \tfrac{28}{60},\ P(\text{both}) = \tfrac{15}{60} :: 60 people. 35 + 28 - 15 = 48 :: Add the totals, then take the overlap away once. P(\text{juice or milk}) = \tfrac{48}{60} :: Everyone inside the circles. P(\text{neither}) = 1 - \tfrac{48}{60} = \tfrac{12}{60} :: Neither is the complement of "or". ``` ### Find the mistake Read Zoe's working. Where are the 4 students with both? ### Or on a dice ## Modify: not, or and neither ```step stage: modify insight: "'Not' and 'or' on the diagram and on a two-dice grid, and 'neither' as the complement of 'or'." try: { playground: board, starter: "board.yml#notmusic", height: 560 } tasks: - starter: "board.yml#notmusic" hint: "Not music is everything outside the Music circle." check: { type: board, text: "Choose the students who do not play music.", when: "x = 1 and w = 1 and y = 0 and z = 0", explain: "Sport only and neither: 12 + 5 = 17, so P(not music) = 17/30 = 1 − 13/30." } - starter: "board.yml#dice" hint: ["A sum over 9 is 10, 11 or 12.", "Doubles run down the diagonal. If you chose the sums over 9 first, two doubles are already chosen."] check: { type: board, text: "Two dice: choose every outcome with a sum over 9 or a double.", when: "r = 1", explain: "6 sums over 9 and 6 doubles, but (5, 5) and (6, 6) are both: 6 + 6 − 2 = 10 outcomes, 10/36." } - check: type: answer q: "30 students: 13 have a dog, 10 have a cat and 4 have both. What is P(neither)?" answer: "11/30" feedback: - ["7/30", "Take the overlap away once: 13 + 10 − 4 = 19 have a dog or a cat."] explain: "Neither is the complement of 'dog or cat': 1 − 19/30 = 11/30." - check: type: question q: "Which means the same as 'at least one of A and B'?" options: ["A and B", "Not A", "Neither", "A or B"] answer: 3 feedback: ["That needs both.", "That ignores B.", "That is none of them.", null] explain: "At least one of them: A, B or both. That is the maths 'or'." ``` ### Not music ### Over 9 or a double ### Neither ### At least one ## Practise: and, or, not ```step stage: practise insight: "Reading and, or, not and exactly one from tables and totals, mixed; counting the overlap twice is the planted slip; exactly one separates the maths or from the everyday one." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "A two-way table of 50 people: 12 wear glasses and are left-handed, 18 wear glasses and are right-handed, 5 are left-handed without glasses, 15 neither. What is P(glasses or left-handed)?" answer: "35/50" feedback: - ["47/50", "The 12 with both are in the glasses count and the left-handed count."] explain: "12 + 18 + 5 = 35, so 35/50 = 7/10." - check: type: answer q: "For the same 50 people, what is P(left-handed and no glasses)?" answer: "5/50" explain: "One cell: 5 of 50 = 1/10." - check: type: number q: "P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A and B) = 0.2. What is P(A or B)?" answer: 0.7 tolerance: 0.001 feedback: - ["0.9", "Take the overlap away once: 0.5 + 0.4 − 0.2."] explain: "0.5 + 0.4 − 0.2 = 0.7." - check: type: answer q: "In the Sport and Music class (12 sport only, 8 both, 5 music only, 5 neither), what is P(exactly one of sport and music)?" answer: "17/30" feedback: - ["25/30", "That is sport or music, which includes the 8 who do both. Exactly one leaves them out."] explain: "Sport only and music only: 12 + 5 = 17, so 17/30. This is the everyday 'one or the other, not both'." ``` ### Glasses or left-handed ### Left-handed, no glasses ### Using the rule ### Exactly one ## Make: an 'or' event ```step stage: make insight: "Building an 'or' event to a given size makes them handle the overlap on purpose." try: { playground: board, starter: "board.yml#make", height: 640 } hint: ["Pick two events that overlap, such as 'the second dice is 1' and 'the sum is 5 or less'.", "Count each, then take away the outcomes in both."] check: { type: board, text: "Two dice: make an event of the form 'A or B', where A and B overlap, with exactly 15 outcomes.", when: "n = 15", explain: "One way: the sum is 9 or more (10 outcomes) or the first dice is 3 (6 outcomes). (3, 6) is in both, so 10 + 6 − 1 = 15." } ``` Write your events A and B in words, and how many outcomes are in A, in B and in both. ## Make: a survey on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A real survey sorts 80 students into four cells; the paper task makes them add the totals and take the overlap away once, and choose that reason." hint: ["Put the 18 in the overlap first.", "Walk only is 38 − 18."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A Year 8 survey asks 80 students two questions. 38 walk to school, 45 play a sport, and 18 do both. How many students walk or play a sport?" steps: - ["Both = 18, and those 18 are in the 38 and in the 45", "the overlap is in both totals"] - ["$38 + 45 - 18 = 65$", "add the totals, then take the overlap away once"] - ["$65$ students walk or play a sport", "everyone inside the circles"] - ["$P = \\tfrac{65}{80}$, and neither is $80 - 65 = 15$", "check: 65 + 15 = 80, the whole year"] picks: - step: 2 q: "What do you do with the 18 who walk and play a sport?" options: - "Add the totals, then take the 18 away once" - "Add the totals: 38 + 45" - "Add the totals and the 18: 38 + 45 + 18" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That counts the 18 twice: they are in both totals.", "That counts them three times. They are already in both totals."] answer: "65" feedback: - ["83", "That adds the totals and counts the 18 twice. Take the overlap away once."] - ["27", "That takes the totals away from each other. Add them first."] criteria: - "I drew a Venn diagram or a table with the 18 in the overlap." - "I took the overlap away once, not twice and not never." - "My 'walk or sport' and 'neither' add up to 80." explain: "38 + 45 − 18 = 65. The 18 are in both totals, so they are taken away once. Neither: 80 − 65 = 15." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The counts are made up, but the question is real: a school asks it to plan buses and sport. Draw a Venn diagram or a two-way table first, then work out how many walk or play, and type your answer. **Also used in** - **Surveys.** A school asks "do you walk, and do you play a sport?" and sorts every answer into the four cells of a two-way table. "Both", "either" and "neither" all read straight off it. - **Weather.** "Will it rain on Friday or Saturday?" is an "or" question, and the next lesson shows how to answer "at least one wet day" by counting the days with none. - **Screening and games.** Medical tests and board games ask "and" and "or" questions, and the overlap is where mistakes creep in. ```teacher summary: Students find P(A and B), P(A or B), P(not A) and P(neither) from Venn diagrams, two-way tables and two-dice grids, counting the overlap once (AC9M8P02, node 2). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 10 min · Modify 12 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can find 'and', 'or', 'not' and 'neither' on a Venn diagram, a table or a grid. - I can work out P(A or B) without counting the overlap twice. - I can explain that 'or' in maths includes both. struggle: The overlap in 'or'. Ask students to point to the overlap and say how many times they have counted it. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need Venn diagrams and two-way tables, grids, and complements (the last three lessons). The one idea: 'and' is the overlap, 'or' is everything inside the circles (one, the other or both), 'not' is outside a circle, and 'neither' is outside both. The common mistake is adding the totals for 'or' (Zoe's mistake), counting the overlap twice. Inclusive 'or' is the maths meaning; everyday 'or' is often exclusive ("tea or coffee?"). Name the difference once. The addition rule P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B) appears as a routine, not a formula to memorise. Wider: Venn diagrams with three circles, and checking 'or' with a complement (neither). running: - "Predict: ask whether a probability can be more than 1." - "Run: ask how many times the 8 are counted now." - "Investigate: ask Zoe where the 4 with both are." - "Modify: ask which outcomes are both over 9 and doubles." - "Make: ask how many outcomes are in A, in B and in both." - "Paper: the survey task is worked in books; the page marks the answer (65) and the reason for taking the overlap away once. Books out, then look at the page for the 18 sitting in the overlap, not the screen." stuck: - see: A student adds the two totals for 'or'. ask: Is anyone in both totals? fix: Add, then take away the overlap once. - see: A student gives 'and' as everyone in either circle. ask: Does 'and' need both to be true? fix: And is the overlap only. - see: A student leaves out the 'both' people from 'or'. ask: Does someone with a dog and a cat have a dog or a cat? fix: In maths, 'or' includes both. stretch: Find P(exactly one of A and B) for the Sport and Music class, and write it using 'or', 'and' and 'not'. support: Four mini Venn diagrams with 'and', 'or', 'not A' and 'neither' shaded, as a reference card. leads: > This completes AC9M8P02. Where it leads: simulations of compound events (next lesson), and independent events in Year 10. exit: q: "40 students: 25 like maths, 18 like art, 10 like both. Find P(maths or art) and P(neither)." a: "25 + 18 − 10 = 33, so 33/40. Neither: 7/40." explain: > **A and B**: both happen (the overlap). **A or B**: at least one happens, both included (everything inside the circles). **Not A**: everything outside A. **Neither**: outside both. Count each outcome once. From totals: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B), because the overlap is in both totals. ```
